title: Conditional probability from letter counts
source: S1 Ch4 theory S1-4.4 Quick check 1 (BANANA, P(N | not A)=2/3)
stem: A letter is selected at random from a word of {n|int} letters, of which {a|int} are the letter A and {k|int} are the letter N. None of the letters N is an A. Find the probability that an N is selected, given that an A is not selected.

steps.name: r
steps.text_tex: There are \({r|int}\) letters that are not A.

contexts.stem: A bag contains {n|int} counters, of which {a|int} are yellow and {k|int} are blue. None of the blue counters is yellow. One counter is selected at random. Find the probability that it is blue, given that it is not yellow.

step_text.r: There are \({r|int}\) names that do not begin with A.

stem: Two counters are selected at random from a bag containing {r|int} red counters and {b|int} blue counters. Find the probability that the second counter is red, given that the first counter is red.

title: Cars in a car park: reduced sample space and independence

source.note: Stem text verbatim from the QP PDF; steps and marks from the official MS PDF (UCLES 2018). Part (iii) is officially accepted either from the formal quotient or directly from the table as 40/90 (reduced sample space, the method of this section). Part (iv) is an independence test (S1-4.3) kept as the official remainder of the question. The official QP table has vertical rules between type columns; those rules are omitted in this stem because the practice checker forbids the | character in task text. Counts and headings are unchanged.

stem:
Last Saturday, Sarah recorded the colour and type of 160 cars in a car park. All the cars that were not red or silver in colour were grouped together as ‘other’. Her results are shown in the following table.
\(\begin{array}{ccccc} & & \text{Saloon} & \text{Hatchback} & \text{Estate} \\ \hline \text{Colour of car} & \text{Red} & 20 & 40 & 12 \\  & \text{Silver} & 14 & 26 & 10 \\  & \text{Other} & 6 & 24 & 8\end{array}\)

parts.stem: Find the probability that a randomly chosen car in the car park is a silver estate car.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen car in the car park is a hatchback car.
Find the probability that a randomly chosen car in the car park is red, given that it is a hatchback car.

steps.name: m
steps.text_tex: Restricted to the 90 hatchbacks, 40 are red, so the probability is \(\dfrac{40}{90}\).
steps.note: MS alternative (direct from table, the method of this section): M1 for 40/a or b/90, a≠160. Official also allows P(red hatchback)/P(hatchback)=(40/160)/(90/160).

steps.name: a
steps.note: MS: A1 4/9 (oe), or 40/90 from the table.

parts.stem: One of the cars in the car park is chosen at random. Determine whether the events ‘the car is a hatchback car’ and ‘the car is red’ are independent, justifying your answer.

steps.name: prod
steps.note: MS: M1 use a correct approach with appropriate probabilities substituted. Alternative: P(red|hatchback)=40/90 ≠ 72/160=P(red).

steps.name: con
steps.note: MS: A1 numerical comparison and conclusion stated.
